title: hand-chart construction grammars (Friedman-canon) vs chi=3 crib cover
hypothesis: K4's >=3 hand-crafted alphabets are built by a systematic mixed-alphabet hand grammar (columnar-mixed / decimation / route) over keyword bases
insights: Construction-grammar pool: 10020 distinct alphabets from 30 keyword-keyed bases x {keyed, columnar-mixed, boustrophedon, diagonal, decimation}. Exact chi=3 (3-alphabet) cover of the 24 cribs: NONE. Greedy needs k=6; best 3 cover 15/23.

PER-METHOD best 3-partial cover (the directional signal): {'keyed': 8, 'columnar': 11, 'boustrophedon': 13, 'diagonal': 10, 'decimation': 15}. Random-alphabet control best 3-partial: 14 (mean 13.0); the 088 memorable pool reached 13/23.
SIGNAL: construction grammars 3-cover 15/23 vs random 14 -- no better than random (no grammar signal).

VERDICT: no 3 construction-grammar alphabets (Friedman columnar-mixed / decimation / route reads over 30 keyword bases) chi=3-cover the cribs, and they cover NO MORE of the cribs than random alphabets do. The 'chart' is not built by any tested systematic hand grammar -- it is genuinely BESPOKE (idiosyncratic per-letter, ~26!^3), recoverable only with the chart itself. This tightens 088: the alphabets are not just 'not memorable', they are not GRAMMAR-constructible either.
next_steps: chart is non-grammar / bespoke -- confirmed not reconstructible from public hand-grammars. Without the sealed chart, the alphabets are in 26!^3 and not deterministically recoverable
